newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British Business Nov 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British Business Nov 24.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
SUNDAY TELEGRAPH

-- CITY FEARS GIVE-AWAY BUDGET Chancellor Kenneth Clarke is facing rising pressure from business leaders for a tight Budget to avoid a further rise in interest rates. The fear is that a tax-cutting Budget not offset by public spending reductions and tax rises will trigger a further rate rise, adding to a sharp rise in sterling's value. This would strike at Britain's competitiveness and exports.
-- BARCLAYS SET TO SELL IMRY TO CHELSFIELD FOR 200 MILLION STG

Barclays Bank is in negotiations with Elliot Bernerd's Chelsfield property group to sell its Imry Holdings for 200 million stg. British Land is also interested in the purchase. Barclay's regarded the company as an investment which would be sold in due course.
-- CARLTON TRUMPS HOLLICK FOR TV STATION

Chairman of Carlton Communications, Michael Green, has bought the privately owned ITV franchise Westcountry Television for 85 million stg, beating the chairman of United News and Media, Lord Hollick, whose offer was accepted on principle. Green's purchase is seen as a defensive move to prevent further expansion by Hollick.
-- FAYED IN ONE MILLION STG-A-YEAR BUSINESS RATES ROW

Following an inquiry by council officers, documents relating to a one million stg-a-year rating dispute involving Mohamed Fayed, owner of Harrods, and Westminster City Council, have been passed to the Inland Revenue's district valuer. Fayed's private company, Hyde Park Residence, runs luxury apartments in Park Lane, which have been charged as being for residential use and have not had to pay the higher business rate to the Council.
-- FUNDS RUSH INTO RENTED PROPERTY
According to investment bank UBS, pension funds and other institutions are set to plough billions into private rented property as returns are expected to soar to 16 per cent a year by 1998.
SUNDAY TIMES

-- GAS TO ATTACK POWER MARKET The trading arm of the gas company to be demerged next year, British Gas Energy, is planning to become one of the leading electricity suppliers to domestic customers when the market is opened to competition in 1998. BGE aims to enter the business at the first opportunity, with the target of supplying about ten per cent of the market's 22 million homes in England and Wales.

-- DESMOND TO BUY SANDY LANE The former stockbroker who owns London City airport, Dermot Desmond, is leading a consortium of Irish investors in the purchase of one of the world's most exclusive hotels, Sandy Lane in Barbados, from Granada Group, for an estimated 40 million stg.
-- POUND LIKELY TO GO HIGHER ON BACK OF ITALY'S RETURN TO ERM

A new clash over Italy's participation in the first wave of European monetary union could develop after the lira's re-entry into the European exchange-rate mechanism. London's Treasury officials said the re-entry would make no difference to the government's position. Britain, Sweden and Greece are the only EU members outside the ERM.
-- T AND N NEAR DEAL TO CAP ASBESTOSIS CLAIMS

The motor components group, T&N, is poised to complete an insurance deal limiting its liability to compensation claims for asbestosis-related disease. This could revitalise T&N's stagnant share price, but could also expose it to a hostile takeover bid. The deal will mean T&N would retain exposure to a liability with a net present value of 300 to 400 million stg.
-- BRITISH AIRWAYS DEAL PUT BACK BY OFT

President of the Board of Trade Ian Lang has referred the terms of the planned British Airways-American Airlines alliance back to the Office of Fair Trading. This is against the wishes to the Department of Transport, which supports the deal. Whitehall officials say Lang does not want to make a ruling that will expose him or the government to criticism.
THE OBSERVER
-- NATIONAL GRID AXES 750 JOBS TO SAVE ONE BILLION STG

The National Grid is set to reveal it will axe 750 jobs in an attempt to save one billion stg over four years. The company blames the cuts on its need to meet price controls imposed by Offer, the electricity regulator. Interim figures will contain encouraging news on Energis, National Grid's telecoms subsidiary, whose losses have been sharply reduced.
-- CONSUMERS' ASSOCIATION 'BEST BUY' CREDIT CARD FAILS TEST OF POPULARITY

Only 1.3 per cent of the Consumers' Association's members have signed up for its new credit card in the three months since its launch. According to a rival operator, a take-up rate of five per cent is deemed respectable, suggesting the CA needs to sign up at least 35,000 cardholders. The venture has been criticised for 'compromising' the association's independence.
-- LONRHO POISED TO SACK WARBURGS WSG.L

Lonrho, the mining and hotels group, is to sack the investment bank SBC Warburg, which it hired to advise on the company's demerger earlier this year. Sources say Warburgs may have overestimated the sum that could be gained from a flotation of the Princess and Metropole hotels, and underestimated interest from direct buyers.
-- NAMES' CAMPAIGN GROUPS FACE NEW BATTLE ON EXPENSES CLAIMS

Lloyd's is to slash 'success fees' for the action groups that waged a five-year battle against the insurance market to gain a rescue for Names. The market has received expenses claims from action group committees tens of millions of pounds stg above the approved limit. Lloyd's say personal payments to committee members will be cut first.
-- BASS DEAL MAY MEAN LOSS OF 2,000 JOBS

According to the Transport and General Workers Union, the proposed merger between Bass and Carlsberg-Tetley is likely to lead to job losses higher than expected. Total redundancies could reach 2,000, representing a quarter of the workforce. The losses will be in distribution and administration. Bass promises no brewery closures.
INDEPENDENT ON SUNDAY
-- LOTTERY FIRM MAY HELP IN FRAUD BATTLE

The Government has been given the opportunity to adopt technology based on that used to run the National Lottery in an attempt to tackle social security fraud and reduce the cost of maintaining the benefits payment system. The lottery computer systems group, GTech, has offered to adapt the electronic welfare distribution system it developed in the U.S. for use in Britain.
-- BOEING'S SUPER-JUMBO TO TAKE OFF FIRST

The "super-jumbo" version of the Boeing 747, capable of carrying 600 passengers, may be purchased by Thai Airways and Malaysian Airlines. This is an important breakthrough in the battle between Boeing and Airbus for supremacy in the aircraft market, which could be worth up to 200 billion dollars.
-- BUILDING SOCIETIES HALT SUBSCRIPTIONS

Building societies, which are seeking conversion, have refused to pay subscriptions to their industry body, the Building Societies Association, after the end of the year. This is further evidence of disenchantment on the part of societies such as the Woolwich, Alliance and Leicester and the Halifax, over the BSA's failure to represent their views to government on new building societies legislation.
-- SALVESEN SELL-OFF PLAN

The Scotland-based distribution and services group, Christian Salvesen, will unveil its plan to float its Aggreko power supply business and pay shareholders a special dividend when it announces its first-half results. The plan is the first stage of efforts to realise more shareholder value for the business since it rebuffed a 1.18 billion stg takeover from Hayes in August.
-- INVESTORS 'STAND BY COOK'

Investors in the castings business, William Cook, are standing by the company. Major shareholders are not prepared to accept a 58.4 million stg hostile bid from engineers Triplex Lloyd. The business has a high concentration of ownership, with seven fund managers owning 60 per cent of shares, the largest being Phillips & Drew, with 21 per cent.
MAIL ON SUNDAY
-- TWIN THREAT TO MORTGAGE RATES

According to the Halifax building society, as mortgages rise homeowners are facing the higher base rates and a threat from the conversion of top building societies into banks. Conversion will force societies to strengthen their appeal to savers, thus driving up home loan rates.
-- BUYERS IN QUEUE FOR 1.6 BILLION STG SEARS

A break up bid worth 1.6 billion stg is imminent for Sears, the retail group. Otto Versand, the world's biggest mail-order company and owner of Grattan in the UK, is discussing the purchase of Sears' Freeman's mail order business for 500 million stg. Also buyers are waiting to takeover Sears' Selfridges department store in London.
-- HEAT IS ON AFTER TUNNEL INFERNO

The Tribunal de Commerce, the French court which is overseeing Eurotunnel's 8.8 billion stg restructuring talks, wants a financial report within the next two weeks. The court has the power to put Eurotunnel into receivership and is worried about the fire's implications for talks with banks.

-- ALERT OVER BANKS ON THE INTERNET The Bank of England has issued a warning over some offshore banks that use the Internet to tempt customers. Officials are worried that UK savers may be lured through advertisements on the World Wide Web. The Bank is concerned about the ease with which overseas operations can beam into British homes, which may lead to more people being tempted into unsafe deposits.
-- ICI POISED TO JOIN THE EXODUS FROM WARBURG WSG.L

ICI may be dropping its merchant bank SBC Warburg. The group is now looking at a short-list of other bankers, including BZW, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Kleinwort Benson and Schroders. Warburg denies it is about to lose ICI and say the group is 100 per cent happy with them.
